description: The single authoritative tuning surface for OpenAxolotl (REQ-025). Every balance value the game uses lives here, never as a constant in system code. Each entry carries a documented name, unit and permitted range; the loader validates against that range and refuses a file that violates it rather than substituting a default.
worldOverridableRationale: A closed set, enumerated here so the Level Contract can reference this list rather than keeping a second one that drifts. Per-world difficulty and restoration economy are legitimately a world's business. Movement, capability, camera and enemy tuning stay global so the game stays coherent across forks.

camera.collision.margin_m.description: How far short of contact geometry the camera stops. The minimum is deliberately above zero: REQ-005 AC-2 requires the camera to NEVER clip into geometry, and a zero margin puts it exactly on the surface where the near plane makes clipping a floating-point coin flip.

camera.follow.land_distance_m.description: Follow distance in the land grammar. Closer than water, which reads as a conventional third-person follow. The gap between the two is what the grammar transition interpolates across, and therefore what the per-frame clamp is measured on.

camera.follow.land_pitch_deg.description: Camera pitch above the axolotl in the land grammar. Higher than water so ledges and hop targets read against the ground.

camera.follow.min_distance_m.description: Floor on how far collision avoidance may pull the camera in. Below this the camera would be inside the axolotl; when geometry demands closer than this, the floor wins and the camera clips rather than turning the view inside out.

camera.follow.water_distance_m.description: Follow distance in the water grammar. Further back than land so the axolotl can pitch and roll in full 3D without the camera chasing every reorientation.

camera.follow.water_pitch_deg.description: Camera pitch above the axolotl in the water grammar. Near level, because underwater the interesting space is ahead rather than below.

camera.look.assist_deg_per_second.description: How fast the idle assist eases the camera back behind travel. Deliberately slower than the player's own turn rate so the assist never feels like it is wrestling the stick. 0.0 disables the assist entirely, leaving the camera wherever the player left it.

camera.look.assist_delay_seconds.description: How long after the player stops touching the look axis before the camera begins easing back behind the direction of travel. Long enough that aiming a jump and then taking it does not have the camera swing mid-air; 0.0 makes the assist immediate, which reintroduces the feedback loop that made a trailing camera and camera-relative movement chase each other.

camera.look.invert_pitch.description: Non-zero inverts the pitch axis, so pushing the stick or mouse forward looks up. A preference rather than a tuning value, and it lives here because there is no options screen yet; when one exists it writes this through the save profile's settings section.

camera.look.max_pitch_deg.description: How far above the axolotl the player may pitch the camera. Generous on purpose: looking down at the level is how a platformer player reads a drop before taking it, and that is the single most useful thing a look axis buys.

camera.look.min_pitch_deg.description: How far below level the player may pitch the camera. Not -89: looking straight up from under the axolotl frames nothing the player can act on, and the orbit would pass through the floor.

camera.look.mouse_deg_per_pixel.description: How far the view turns per pixel of mouse motion. The whole look axis: without it the camera only trailed the direction of travel and a jump could not be aimed. Sensitivity is per-pixel rather than per-frame so a flick means the same at any frame rate.

camera.look.stick_deadzone.description: Stick magnitude below which look input is ignored, applied to the vector's LENGTH rather than per axis so a diagonal push does not have to clear the threshold twice. Past it the rate is rescaled from the edge, so the first movement is slow rather than a jump to full speed.

camera.look.stick_deg_per_second.description: Turn rate at full stick deflection. Rate-based rather than displacement-based, because that is what a stick means: held over, it keeps turning. A full 180-degree turn takes a second, which is quick enough to catch a gap behind you and slow enough to aim.

camera.smoothing.max_position_delta_m_pe.description: Hard per-frame clamp on camera position change, including across a grammar transition. A clamp rather than a lerp factor, so the bound holds at any frame rate.

camera.smoothing.max_rotation_delta_deg_.description: Hard per-frame clamp on camera rotation change, including across a grammar transition.

camera.smoothing.position_damping_per_se.description: Exponential damping rate for the camera's follow distance. Applied as 1-exp(-rate*delta) so the tuned number means the same thing at any frame rate. The per-frame clamp above is a separate, harder bound; this only sets how briskly the camera converges within it.

camera.smoothing.rotation_damping_per_se.description: Exponential damping rate for camera pitch and yaw. Slightly brisker than position: a camera that lags in angle reads as unresponsive faster than one that lags in distance.

capability.gill_loss.boost_duration_mult.description: Bubble-boost duration while a gill is lost.

capability.leg_loss.climb_height_multipl.description: Reachable climb height while a leg is lost. Multiplies controller.climb.max_height_m.

capability.tail_loss.swim_speed_multipli.description: Swim speed while the tail is lost. Capability loss degrades traversal; it never ends a run on its own. The minimum is above zero on purpose: REQ-002 AC-3 rests on a product of strictly positive factors, so every capability lost still leaves the axolotl able to move.

collectibles.resource_pickup_value.description: Restoration resources one resource-kind collectible delivers to its declared region when picked up. Read at pickup time by the Collectibles System, never cached. A world's restoration economy is this value times its placed pickups against the region costs, so raising it makes every world's restoration cheaper at once; per-world economy belongs in the overridable resource costs instead.

combat.spin_sprint.reach_m.description: How far from the axolotl a spinning body knocks a machine out. Measured from the body's centre, so it is roughly a body length: the spin has to CONNECT, not merely happen nearby.

combat.stomp.bounce_m_per_s.description: The upward kick off a stomped machine. Below the hop impulse on purpose: a bounce that beat a jump would make enemies the best way up, and this is a reward for landing the hit, not a traversal route.

combat.stomp.reach_m.description: How close beneath the axolotl a machine has to be for a landing to count as a stomp. Landing ON a thing is a platformer's oldest verb and the one players try first, so the radius is forgiving.

combat.tail_whack.cooldown_s.description: Rest between swings, so the land strike is a swing rather than a held button.

combat.tail_whack.reach_m.description: How far the tail whack reaches. Longer than the spin's radius because the tail is the axolotl's longest part and swinging it is the whole point.

combat.tail_whack.window_s.description: How long the swing is live. The strike lands once, on the frame the window opens; the window is what stops the player steering out of the animation and what the clip is timed against.

controller.bubble_boost.cooldown_s.description: Recovery window after a bubble boost ends, during which it cannot be re-activated. The minimum is deliberately above zero: REQ-001 AC-2 requires the boost to be GOVERNED by a cooldown, so a tuning file that zeroes it must fail to load rather than quietly producing an ungoverned boost.

controller.bubble_boost.duration_s.description: How long a bubble boost multiplies swim speed. Scaled down by capability.gill_loss.boost_duration_multiplier while a gill is lost.

controller.bubble_boost.speed_multiplier.description: Swim speed multiplier while a bubble boost is active.

controller.climb.adhesion_m_per_s.description: Speed pushed INTO the climbable surface every frame while attached. The body ends a climb the moment it stops touching the wall, and a climber moving purely along the surface generates no contact -- so without this the climb detaches on its second frame. move_and_slide absorbs the component against the wall, so it costs no movement. Raise it if a climber pops off a bumpy or curved surface; 0.0 disables it and restores the detaching behaviour.

controller.climb.contact_grace_seconds.description: How long a climber may keep the wall after the body stops touching it. A seam or a curve in a surface drops the capsule clear for a frame or two, and cresting a lip loses contact while the feet are still below it -- without this grace both end the climb and drop the player the whole way back down. Like coyote time it changes no reachable height, only how much precision the geometry demands. 0.0 restores the strict frame-by-frame release.

controller.climb.max_height_m.description: How far the axolotl can rise on a single climbable surface, measured from where it attached. Multiplied by capability.leg_loss.climb_height_multiplier, which is what makes REQ-002's 'leg reduces climb height' a measurable number rather than a claim. At the ceiling the climber can still move sideways and descend.

controller.climb.speed_m_per_s.description: Movement speed while attached to a climbable surface. Deliberately NOT scaled by leg loss: a lost leg lowers how high the axolotl can reach, not how fast it climbs.

controller.dash.max_charges.description: Water-powered dash charges held at once. The dash is usable in both grammars but recharges only in water.

controller.dash.recharge_seconds_per_cha.description: Time submerged to regain one dash charge. Does not accrue on land.

controller.dive.acceleration_m_per_s2.description: How fast a dive or a surface reaches its target vertical speed. A dive used to SET velocity.y outright, which snapped the axolotl downward in one frame and read as a teleport rather than a movement; easing into it is what makes the descent a glide. At this rate full dive speed arrives in about an eighth of a second — visibly a movement, and quick enough that the flown Coral Cove route still makes every jump. THERE IS A FLOOR HERE AND IT IS MEASURED: at 22 the swim timing shifted enough to compound into a missed lateral jump forty legs later, and the route lost a life to the gorge. Lower this and re-fly the coral walk before believing it.

controller.dive.speed_m_per_s.description: Descent rate of a deliberate dive. A dive sets the vertical component outright rather than adding to steering, so diving from a standstill still descends.

controller.facing.turn_rate_deg_per_s.description: How fast the axolotl's body swings to face its direction of travel. Fast enough that a reversal reads as a flick rather than a slow pivot, slow enough that the turn is visible: an instant snap makes the character look teleported.

controller.grapple.arrival_radius_m.description: Distance at which an attached grapple counts as arrived and detaches. Without a radius the pull would oscillate around the anchor forever.

controller.grapple.max_range_m.description: Maximum tongue-grapple anchor distance. Tested inclusively: an anchor exactly at this range attaches, one beyond it is rejected.

controller.grapple.pull_speed_m_per_s.description: Speed at which an attached grapple pulls the axolotl toward its anchor. Faster than swimming, so the grapple reads as a traversal shortcut rather than a slow winch.

controller.gravity.land_m_per_s2.description: Downward acceleration applied by the scene-tree body while the land grammar is active and the axolotl is neither climbing nor grappling. Higher than real gravity on purpose: a platformer hop that follows a 9.81 arc reads as floaty, and the hop impulse is tuned against this number rather than against physics.

controller.gravity.terminal_speed_m_per_.description: Maximum downward speed gravity may accumulate. Bounds a long fall so a pit plunge stays readable and cannot tunnel through thin floor collision.

controller.gravity.water_m_per_s2.description: Downward drift while swimming. 0.0 is neutral buoyancy, which is the intended feel: an axolotl holds its depth and the vertical axis belongs entirely to steering. Raise it to make water sink the player when they stop steering.

controller.hop.buffer_seconds.description: How long a hop pressed in mid-air is remembered and fired on landing. Without it, chaining a jump immediately on touchdown requires hitting the exact landing frame. Remembered on the rising edge only, so holding the button does not refill it.

controller.hop.coyote_seconds.description: How long after walking off a ledge a hop still fires. Players press jump a few frames LATE far more often than early, and without this those presses vanish silently. 0.0 disables coyote time and restores the strict grounded-only hop.

controller.hop.impulse_m_per_s.description: Upward velocity a hop imparts. Only available while grounded (or inside the coyote window), so a hop cannot be chained in mid-air. With the land gravity of 20 m/s^2 this gives a 2.03 m peak and 0.90 s of airtime, which is the arc every gap and ledge height in the official worlds is measured against -- changing it invalidates those clearances, so the reachability probe re-derives them from this value rather than hard-coding distances.

controller.hop.release_cut_ratio.description: Fraction of the RISING vertical speed kept when the player releases the hop button mid-climb. This is what makes one button express a range of heights, so a level can ask for a small hop onto a low ledge and a full leap across a gap without a second verb. 1.0 disables the cut and every jump reaches full height.

controller.pitch.full_speed_m_per_s.description: The vertical speed at which the model reaches controller.pitch.max_deg. Deliberately the dive speed, so a full dive is a full nose-down and everything gentler is proportional.

controller.pitch.max_deg.description: How far the model noses down or up at full vertical speed. Visual only, like facing: the capsule never rotates. Past about fifty degrees the tail swings through the ground on a shallow seabed, which is why this stops well short of vertical.

controller.pitch.rate_deg_per_s.description: How fast the model's pitch chases the pitch its vertical speed asks for. Chased rather than set for the same reason the heading is: an instantaneous match makes every ripple in vertical speed a visible flick of the whole body.

controller.roll.cooldown_s.description: Rest between rolls, measured from the end of one to the start of the next. Without it, holding the key turns a dodge into the fastest way across a level and the waddle stops mattering.

controller.roll.duration_s.description: How long the roll drives the body. Short: the roll is a commitment, and every frame of it is a frame the player is not steering.

controller.roll.speed_m_per_s.description: Ground speed of the sideways dodge roll. Faster than a waddle by more than double, or the roll would be a way of walking rather than a way of getting out of the way.

controller.spin_sprint.cooldown_s.description: Rest between spin sprints. Longer than the roll's because the spin also lands a strike, and a strike on tap is a strike with no timing in it.

controller.spin_sprint.duration_s.description: How long the spin sprint drives. Long enough to cross a Netbot's reach, short enough that it cannot be used as a swim speed.

controller.spin_sprint.speed_m_per_s.description: Speed of the underwater spin sprint. Above the bubble boost's peak, because the boost is a sustained cruise and this is a lunge — and because it is the water grammar's strike, so it has to close distance on a machine that is holding station.

controller.squash.hop_stretch.description: How much taller the model stretches at the start of a hop, as a fraction of its rest height; width shrinks to keep the volume. Visual only. 0.0 disables the stretch.

controller.squash.land_squash.description: How much shorter the model squashes on landing, as a fraction of its rest height; width grows to keep the volume. Visual only. 0.0 disables the squash.

controller.squash.recover_rate_per_s.description: Exponential rate at which a squash or stretch returns to rest. 10.0 recovers most of the way in a quarter of a second: quick enough to read as rubber, slow enough that a hop visibly stretches before the arc.

controller.surface.acceleration_m_per_s2.description: The same easing for rising. Slower than the dive on purpose: an axolotl drops with gravity behind it and climbs against buoyancy, so surfacing that eased as hard as diving read as a lift rather than a swim. Constrained by the flown route the same way the dive is.

controller.swim.base_speed_m_per_s.description: Base swim speed under full 3D directional steering, before capability modifiers and the bubble boost multiplier.

controller.swim.drag_per_second.description: How briskly a swimming axolotl sheds speed when the player is not steering. An order of magnitude gentler than the land drag: water is the grammar that GLIDES, and that contrast is a large part of what makes the two read as mechanically distinct. Also bounds a fall into water, which would otherwise sink at its entry speed until it hit the floor.

controller.transition.momentum_retention.description: Fraction of speed magnitude retained when crossing a water/land boundary. Applied to magnitude, not the vector, so a surfacing swimmer keeps speed without keeping an underwater heading.

controller.waddle.base_speed_m_per_s.description: Base grounded waddle speed. Still well below the swim speed -- water is the fast grammar and that gap is what makes the two read as distinct -- but fast enough that a jump covers useful ground: at the tuned arc it yields 3.78 m of horizontal reach, which is what makes gap jumping a real verb rather than a hop in place.

controller.waddle.drag_per_second.description: How briskly a grounded axolotl sheds horizontal speed when the player is not steering. Applied as exp(-rate*delta) so the tuned number means the same at any frame rate. High relative to the swim drag: land should feel planted, and releasing the key should stop you almost at once. The minimum is deliberately above zero -- at zero the axolotl would coast forever and walk off the level, which is a bug rather than a tuning choice.

enemy.disabled_seconds.description: How long a struck Drift Fleet machine stays knocked out: its effect is refused, and whatever it was already doing to the player is released. It recovers rather than being destroyed — these are machines being knocked over, not things being killed (REQ-019), and a permanent removal would let a player empty a level and walk it unopposed.

enemy.hookline.mod_strip_seconds.description: Window for which a Hookline Rig snag strips the equipped Gill Mod.

enemy.netbot.entangle_seconds.description: Entanglement duration if the player does not counter with Jet Gills.

enemy.netbot.swim_speed_multiplier.description: Swim speed while entangled in a Netbot ghost net.

enemy.runoff.duration_s.description: How long the Runoff Drone debuff persists after leaving the toxin volume.

enemy.runoff.gill_recharge_multiplier.description: Gill recharge rate multiplier while inside a Runoff Drone toxin volume.

enemy.runoff.vision_debuff_factor.description: Vision range multiplier while inside a Runoff Drone toxin volume.

gillmod.bubble.cooldown_s.description: Cooldown after the Bubble Gill mod deactivates.

gillmod.bubble.duration_s.description: Active duration of the Bubble Gill mod.

gillmod.glow.cooldown_s.description: Cooldown after the Glow Gill mod deactivates.

gillmod.glow.duration_s.description: Active duration of the Glow Gill mod, which reveals Hookline Rig lines in murk.

gillmod.jet.cooldown_s.description: Cooldown after the Jet Gill mod deactivates.

gillmod.jet.duration_s.description: Active duration of the Jet Gill mod, the counter to Netbot entanglement.

progression.default_lives_per_attempt.description: Lives granted at the start of an attempt. Lives are spent only on catastrophic events, never on ordinary capability loss.

progression.max_retry_seconds.description: Upper bound from losing a life to being playable again at the last checkpoint.

regen.mutation.duration_s.description: How long a mutated regrowth loadout persists before reverting to the baseline form.

restoration.resourced.resource_cost.description: Restoration resources consumed to advance a region from barren to resourced.

restoration.restored.resource_cost.description: Restoration resources consumed to advance a region from resourced to restored.
